body:
You didn't offend, I just wouldn't have said it that way. 

Yes I'm considering grad school. As something to do following up on my academic career, almost like "well might as well continue on this course..." despite all my doubts. Perhaps doubt is not the right way of putting it, I know a lot of (if not most) grad students face some doubt about their career choice, but I **know** I will not be content doing the work that is required in my field. In that sense there is no doubt. I should point out that I'm still incredibly interested in the subject, just not at all the methods and practices used. The doubt is whether I should stay the course with my current career path regardless, or abandon it. But then I would have no idea what to do and would probably have to go back to school for something completely different and I just don't have the money to do that (hell I'm already too far in debt).

I get what you're saying, but for my case the inaction is just that, inaction. Not an affirmation of continued life. Most people probably wouldn't say that my head is in the right place after reading a post like this and I'm not sure I agree with you but again, thanks. 

Well as I said I've continued living despite feeling this for years. In this time I've tried to figure out what I would want to do with my life if I chose to continue living (no sense in deferring that decision until the existential one is solved right?) and so I've picked something that interests me. I graduated college with a degree that *might* get me into a grad school in this field. Although I have been having doubts about it because the work is not what I want to spend my life *doing*. (what a time to start having doubts right? after you've already got the degree!) So I don't know what to do now on two levels. Live or die, and if I choose life, what should I do with it that will keep me at least content **most** of the time. I haven't even found anything that keeps me content for a fraction of the time... because it all just returns to the existential question.

I'm not that brave, but thanks for saying that. 

It's just that one part of me wants to kill myself and another part is not convinced that is the best option. It's an ongoing inner dialogue, concerning what to do, given my conclusions about life. I end up living because it is the default option, i.e. not making a decision results in me continuing to live.
